method_selection.citation: Bergstra & Bengio, JMLR 2012 (random search); Li et al. 2018 (Hyperband/ASHA successive halving)
method_selection.why: Validation peaks at epoch 8 (0.601838) and then declines while training loss reaches its minimum, indicating overfitting. With 15 iterations left and no convergence strike, a broad short-probe search over weight decay, embedding size, learning rate, dropout where applicable, and checkpoint choice has greater scientific value than a narrow treatment. It directly searches the regularization and capacity balance needed for this small dataset and can reserve budget to fully train the winning configuration.

rejected.reason: It matches the pathology, but it is a narrower hand-selected package; the random-search card can screen these same regularization and schedule dials plus capacity and checkpoint choice.
Added interaction capacity is poorly matched to the observed overfitting and is risky on this small dataset before regularization and capacity dials are established.
The temporal split makes it plausible, but the supplied learning curve directly demonstrates overfitting rather than temporal degradation.
Its metric-mismatch or flat-signal diagnoses are not supported by the steadily improving validation ranking before the late decline.
This is a closing move requiring an established, tuned champion and exhaustion of promising single-model moves; the run is only at its first post-baseline iteration.
Final-stage preconditions are not met, and training several models now would be premature.
Single-model opportunities have not plateaued and no distinct competitive families have yet been measured in this run.

expected_delta_basis: Bergstra and Bengio (2012) support wide random search when only a subset of dials matter, Li et al. (2018) support successive pruning, and node_000's measured post-peak decline specifically indicates an untuned capacity-regularization balance.

method_selection.why: Validation peaks at epoch 8 (0.601838) and then declines while training loss reaches its minimum, indicating overfitting. With 15 iterations left and no convergence strike, a broad short-probe search over weight decay, embedding size, learning rate, dropout where applicable, and checkpoint choice has greater scientific value than a narrow treatment. It directly searches the regularization and capacity balance needed for this small dataset and can reserve budget to fully train the winning configuration.

rejected.reason: It matches the pathology, but it is a narrower hand-selected package; the random-search card can screen these same regularization and schedule dials plus capacity and checkpoint choice.
Added interaction capacity is poorly matched to the observed overfitting and is risky on this small dataset before regularization and capacity dials are established.
The temporal split makes it plausible, but the supplied learning curve directly demonstrates overfitting rather than temporal degradation.
Its metric-mismatch or flat-signal diagnoses are not supported by the steadily improving validation ranking before the late decline.
This is a closing move requiring an established, tuned champion and exhaustion of promising single-model moves; the run is only at its first post-baseline iteration.
Final-stage preconditions are not met, and training several models now would be premature.
Single-model opportunities have not plateaued and no distinct competitive families have yet been measured in this run.
